verdict.rationale: Pipecat ships its own scriptable surfaces that suit automation. The official CLI ran keylessly via uvx and exposes init, cloud deploy and eval commands. Pipecat Evals runs described conversations against the real agent and reports whether expectations hold, and the Cloud REST API (OpenAPI spec) manages agents, builds and secrets programmatically. However, no documentation explicitly covers headless or CI use, and the dev runner is local-only and serves a UI. Missing for 10: explicit headless/CI usage docs (e.g. CI pipeline examples, non-interactive flags, exit codes for evals), independent corroboration of running in CI.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: the official Pipecat CLI (pypi pipecat-ai[cli]) ran keylessly via uvx
Pipecat Evals is the framework's built-in system for testing agent behavior.
Pipecat runs it against your real agent (the same pipeline, the same services, the same code) and tells you whether the expectation still holds.
The private API (/v1...) manages agents, secrets, builds, regions, and organization settings.
